title: Motion and colour-independence regression guards
description:
Objective: lock in the two spec section 11.1 guarantees that are currently true only by accident, so they cannot silently regress.

READ THIS FIRST — THIS GAP IS MUCH SMALLER THAN ITS NAME. It was opened as "prefers-reduced-motion is unimplemented". That was WRONG, and an adversarial refutation pass confirmed the correction. Measured on disk:
- board-layout.css:68 ALREADY has @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce), containing scroll-behavior:auto (line 70), animation:none (74) and transition:none (75).
- goals-board-ban.test.ts:147 ALREADY pins that block as source text.
- THERE IS NO MOTION TO SUPPRESS. Exhaustive inventory across apps/control-room and the control-room packages: @keyframes 0, transform 0, requestAnimationFrame 0, setTimeout/setInterval 0, spinner/fade/slide/easing/cubic-bezier/duration/opacity 0. Exactly one .css file exists (77 lines). It has one transition: declaration, value none, and one animation: declaration, value none — both inside the reduced-motion block, i.e. suppressing motion that does not exist. The three skeletons (cr.board.skeleton, cr.goals.skeleton, cr.health.skeleton) are empty divs with no CSS rule at all. The only declarations that move anything in a real browser are scroll-snap-type and scroll-snap-align, already neutralised by scroll-behavior:auto.
- All three cr.banner.* ids that exist are ALREADY live regions: disconnected (frame.tsx:132) and lag (frame.tsx:139) via role="status", invalidated (approval-detail-plan.tsx:187) via aria-live="polite". The three the spec names that lack one — circuitbreaker, revision, refusal — do not exist as components at all.

A worker who starts adding a useReducedMotion hook, transition-suppression CSS, or a motion token layer is building suppressors for motion that does not exist. A worker who tries to "add aria-live to the banners that lack it" will find nothing to fix and may invent placeholder banners — a stub carrying a real cr.banner.* id is exactly the dishonesty the frame already guards against for cr.graph.*. Confirm the zero counts yourself first.

THE REAL DELIVERABLE is two regression guards plus one tightening:
1. Pin the motion inventory at zero, so the reduced-motion guarantee cannot be quietly falsified by a future stylesheet.
2. Assert the non-chip half of section 11.1 bullet 1 ("no colour-only encoding anywhere") against real renders. Only the truth-chip fragment is covered today, by auditTruthClassMonochrome. The board's own overlays and indicators are not.
3. Tighten gating-keyboard.test.tsx:102, which currently accepts role "status" OR "alert" for cr.banner.disconnected, where section 11.1 line 687 says banners announce POLITELY.

Owned paths: apps/control-room/src/a11y/** (new test files only) and apps/control-room/src/shell/gating-keyboard.test.tsx.

Hard dependencies: Accessibility latency hardening (task-ab8c9489ab6446c384e977a3e1cc8063) must reach DONE first — it owns src/a11y/** and is WORKING.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test
definitionOfDone: A source-text test pins the motion inventory at zero across every .css and .tsx under apps/control-room/src: it asserts the scanned file set is NON-EMPTY first, then that no file contains @keyframes, no transition: or animation: declaration with a value other than none, and no scroll-behavior: smooth. It MUST NOT ban scroll-snap-type or scroll-snap-align — board-layout.css uses both legitimately for spec section 4.16 column behavior, and banning them would fight the narrow-mode tasks.

The same test asserts every .css file under apps/control-room/src contains a @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block, and pins the existing block's contents (animation: none, transition: none, scroll-behavior: auto) so it cannot be deleted or hollowed out silently.

The non-chip half of section 11.1 bullet 1 is asserted against REAL rendered surfaces, not fragments: every rendered board card overlay, badge and indicator conveys its meaning in text or glyph and not by colour alone. Assert the swept element count is greater than zero before asserting zero violations, and report each violation with a stable reason code naming the offending test id.

gating-keyboard.test.tsx no longer accepts role="alert" for cr.banner.disconnected: each of the three existing banner ids is asserted to resolve to a POLITE live region (role="status" or aria-live="polite", never assertive/alert), per section 11.1 line 687.

Recorded as explicit not-applicable WITH the reason, never as a passing assertion over zero cases: (a) WCAG AA contrast — no colour value exists anywhere to measure. TruthSemanticTone is a prose union ("neutral slate", "amber"), the one stylesheet uses only the system keywords canvas and highlight, and there are zero hex/rgb/hsl/oklch literals in the app or any package. This needs a colour-token layer and is a separate task whose DoD cannot be written until tones resolve to values. (b) The graph half of bullet 1 (edges use pattern + arrowheads, critical path uses weight + pattern) — no graph surface exists; note that criticalPath already renders as a text SuppliedFact via board-card.tsx:43, so it is not colour-only today. (c) cr.banner.circuitbreaker, cr.banner.revision and cr.graph.refusal — those components do not exist, and no placeholder may be created to satisfy a sweep.

pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test passes, and each new guard is verified by mutating the production surface — add a transition to the stylesheet, and strip a badge's text label — confirming each guard goes red, then reverting.
taskRails: Pinned UI spec: D:/projexts/moes/docs/plans/2026-08-05-moe-v1-control-room-spec.md SHA-256 C55AF8A9FC7386E6492FD57E34A4B8321ABAAE4E4E08FF38703544B58B0BEF1F. Section 11.1 is lines 681-687.

Do NOT add production code to satisfy this task. Its own measurement is that zero production changes are required: the reduced-motion block exists, there is no motion to suppress, and every banner that exists is already a live region. If you find yourself writing a hook or a stylesheet, re-read the description and confirm the zero counts before proceeding.

NEVER create a component just to give a sweep something to find. cr.banner.circuitbreaker, cr.banner.revision and cr.graph.refusal do not exist. A stub carrying a real cr.banner.* id would be a fabricated surface — exactly what the frame already refuses to do for cr.graph.*.

Do not reimplement auditLiveRegions, auditTruthClassMonochrome or any other predicate in apps/control-room/src/a11y/surface-audit.ts — consume them. Locate symbols by NAME, never by line number: that file is actively changing and every line number recorded here will be stale.

jsdom 30.0.1 implements neither window.matchMedia nor media-query evaluation, and document.styleSheets.length is 0 because Vitest stubs the CSS import. No assertion may be driven by an actual prefers-reduced-motion match. The motion guard is a source-text pin and must be labelled as one.
Do not assert a global test COUNT as a completion signal. This is a shared worktree with other agents adding tests; a total-count assertion is not a property of this task and will drift.
Keep each file below 400 lines, target 250. Explicit owned paths only; no git add -A.
